verdict.rationale: The SDK documents sandboxed execution: Sandbox agents run inside real isolated workspaces with manifest-defined files, and the CodeInterpreterTool executes code in a sandboxed environment. On the permissions side, the only documented control is approval gating, where a tool call that requires approval pauses the run until someone resumes it. Guardrails validate input and output but are not tool permissions. Missing for 10: documented fine-grained per-tool allow/deny permission policies or scopes, details on sandbox isolation boundaries and restrictions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can restrict what an agent may do with fine-grained tool permissions and sandboxed execution

citations.quote: Sandbox agents: Run specialists inside real isolated workspaces.
The CodeInterpreterTool lets the LLM execute code in a sandboxed environment.
When a tool call requires approval, the SDK pauses the run, returns `interruptions`, and lets you resume later from the same `RunState`.
If the agent should run inside an isolated workspace with manifest-defined files and sandbox-native capabilities, read Sandbox agent concepts.
